draft:
We did not speak of guilt at birth, but we believed something real went wrong at the root of humanity [[alx.dw.original-sin]] [[as:paraphrase]]. Adam's fall cast its shadow over every soul, and death and disorder came down to all of us [[alx.dw.original-sin]] [[as:paraphrase]]. No one reached God unwounded [[alx.dw.original-sin]] [[as:paraphrase]].

Our teachers spoke of inherited death and weakness, and also of a fall that each soul signs onto in its own living [[alx.dw.original-sin]] [[as:paraphrase]]. The wound was real, universal, and inherited in its effects, and the doctor's imagery outweighed the courtroom's [[alx.dw.original-sin]] [[as:paraphrase]]. Origen wondered about the soul's own descent, but as open inquiry, not doctrine [[alx.dw.original-sin]] [[as:paraphrase]].

The doctor's image runs through our witness to Jesus, whose death is the doctor entering the sickness [[alx.dw.jesus]] [[as:paraphrase]]. The resurrection, the anastasis, meant death reversed in both kinds: the soul reunited with God, and the body truly transformed [[alx.term.anastasis]] [[as:paraphrase]].
